scenes.visual: Title card 'Similar Bodies, Different Branches' fades in over two pale worm silhouettes side by side. THE WORLD, kept for both films (16:9, warm cream background, simple flat cartoons, no molecular structures). COLOUR MAP, same in every scene and in the second film: ectoderm / outer layer BLUE; mesoderm / middle layer and muscle ORANGE; endoderm / gut lining YELLOW; gut lumen WHITE; coelomic or body-cavity fluid PALE CYAN; Spiralia branch GREEN; Ecdysozoa branch PURPLE; Deuterostomia branch GREY. Names fixed: nematode, earthworm, planarian, coelom, septa. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: A nematode and an earthworm look almost the same. Are they close relatives? Both are soft, tube-shaped worms. Each has a gut that runs from mouth to anus.
scenes.visual: A thin cream nematode and a pink ringed earthworm wriggle side by side, labelled 'nematode' and 'earthworm'. A white line runs through each from a 'mouth' label to an 'anus' label. A question mark pulses between them.
scenes.narration: A nematode and an earthworm look almost the same. Are they close relatives? Both are soft, tube-shaped worms. Each has a gut that runs from mouth to anus.

scenes.tts: Slice each worm across the middle. Add a third worm, a flat planarian. Now colour the tissue layers. The outer layer is blue. The middle layer, mesoderm, is orange. It makes muscle. The gut lining is yellow.
scenes.visual: A knife line cuts each worm; a round cross-section swings out beside each. A flat planarian slides in on the left and is sliced too. Three cross-sections in a row, labelled 'planarian', 'nematode', 'earthworm'. Layers fill in as each colour is named: BLUE ring outside, ORANGE layer inside it, YELLOW ring around a WHITE centre. Small label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Slice each worm across the middle. Add a third worm, a flat planarian. Now colour the tissue layers. The outer layer is blue. The middle layer, mesoderm, is orange. It makes muscle. The gut lining is yellow.

scenes.tts: The small white space in each centre is the gut lumen, where food goes. It is not the body cavity. The body cavity, if there is one, lies between gut and body wall.
scenes.visual: A pointer circles the WHITE centre of each section; label 'gut lumen (food)'. Then a dashed ring highlights the zone between YELLOW gut and BLUE wall in each; label 'body cavity?'.
scenes.narration: The small white space in each centre is the gut lumen, where food goes. It is not the body cavity. The body cavity, if there is one, lies between gut and body wall.

scenes.tts: In the planarian, tissue fills that space. There is no body cavity. In the nematode, a fluid space is lined by mesoderm only on the outside. That is a pseudocoelom.
scenes.visual: Planarian section: ORANGE tissue fills the zone solidly; label 'acoelomate: no cavity'. Nematode section: the zone fills with PALE CYAN fluid; an ORANGE lining draws along the body-wall side only, none against the YELLOW gut; label 'pseudocoelom'.
scenes.narration: In the planarian, tissue fills that space. There is no body cavity. In the nematode, a fluid space is lined by mesoderm only on the outside. That is a pseudocoelom.

scenes.tts: In the earthworm, the fluid space is lined by mesoderm on both sides. That is a true coelom. Three worms, three ways to fill the same space.
scenes.visual: Earthworm section: PALE CYAN fluid fills the zone; ORANGE lining draws along both the body wall and the outside of the gut; label 'coelom'. All three sections glow briefly together.
scenes.narration: In the earthworm, the fluid space is lined by mesoderm on both sides. That is a true coelom. Three worms, three ways to fill the same space.

scenes.tts: Libbie Hyman's great survey of the invertebrates ordered animals this way. No cavity, then a partial lining, then a full one. It looks like a staircase, from simple to complex.
scenes.visual: The three sections lift onto three ascending steps: planarian bottom, nematode middle, earthworm top. Step labels 'no cavity', 'partial lining', 'full lining'. A caption 'Hyman: The Invertebrates' at the top of the stairs. An arrow up the stairs labelled 'simple to complex?'.
scenes.narration: Libbie Hyman's great survey of the invertebrates ordered animals this way. No cavity, then a partial lining, then a full one. It looks like a staircase, from simple to complex.

scenes.tts: Now compare genes from many animals instead. If the staircase were a family tree, where should the nematode land? Between the flatworm and the earthworm, or somewhere else?
scenes.visual: The staircase fades to an outline. A strand of DNA letters scrolls across the top labelled 'many genes'. The nematode section hovers above the stairs with a question mark; two dotted landing spots: 'between?' on the middle step and '?' off to the side.
scenes.narration: Now compare genes from many animals instead. If the staircase were a family tree, where should the nematode land? Between the flatworm and the earthworm, or somewhere else?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question holds. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Somewhere else. The genes put the nematode with the arthropods, such as insects. Both shed a tough outer cuticle as they grow. That moulting names the group, Eck-dih-so-ZO-uh.
scenes.caption: Somewhere else. The genes put the nematode with the arthropods, such as insects. Both shed a tough outer cuticle as they grow. That moulting names the group, Ecdysozoa.
scenes.visual: The staircase redraws into a branching tree. The nematode slides off the middle step to a new branch beside a cartoon insect labelled 'arthropod'. A thin outer skin peels off both and drops away; label 'moulting (ecdysis)'. Their shared branch turns PURPLE; label 'Ecdysozoa'.
scenes.narration: Somewhere else. The genes put the nematode with the arthropods, such as insects. Both shed a tough outer cuticle as they grow. That moulting names the group, Ecdysozoa.

scenes.tts: The planarian moves too. It lands beside the earthworm and a snail, in a group called Spiralia. Its relatives have a coelom. So the flatworm is not an early, simple branch.
scenes.visual: The planarian drops off the bottom step onto a branch beside the earthworm and a cartoon snail; that branch turns GREEN, label 'Spiralia'. Nearby, a GREY bracket (not a solid branch) holds a sea urchin and a fish silhouette, label 'Deuterostomia (traditional; support debated)'. Struck-through label 'early, simple branch' fades next to the planarian.
scenes.narration: The planarian moves too. It lands beside the earthworm and a snail, in a group called Spiralia. Its relatives have a coelom. So the flatworm is not an early, simple branch.

scenes.tts: Now mark each tip with its body cavity. The cavity marks are scattered across the tree. The moulting mark sits on one branch only.
scenes.visual: Each tip gets a tiny cross-section icon: solid ORANGE (no cavity), half-lined PALE CYAN (pseudocoelom), fully lined PALE CYAN (coelom). Coelom icons appear on GREEN, PURPLE and GREY branches; the pseudocoelom sits inside PURPLE; no-cavity inside GREEN. A single PURPLE tick labelled 'moulting' sits on the base of the Ecdysozoa branch. No numbers.
scenes.narration: Now mark each tip with its body cavity. The cavity marks are scattered across the tree. The moulting mark sits on one branch only.

scenes.tts: Animals that share a level of organization, like a body-cavity type, form a grade. A clade is something else. It is an ancestor and all of its descendants.
scenes.visual: Left panel: the three staircase sections boxed together, label 'grade: same level of organization'. Right panel: the PURPLE branch with its base node circled and every tip above it highlighted, label 'clade: ancestor + all descendants'.
scenes.narration: Animals that share a level of organization, like a body-cavity type, form a grade. A clade is something else. It is an ancestor and all of its descendants.

scenes.tts: A shared, derived character can mark a clade. It is a new state that arose in a common ancestor. Moulting fits one origin on this tree. Cavity type changes several times. To test any character, lay it on a tree built from other evidence. Many genes are one such source.
scenes.visual: A checklist card: 'shared, derived: one origin on a tree built from other evidence?'. Beside 'moulting' a PURPLE tick; beside 'cavity type' a cross, with the scattered icons flashing. Then a DNA strand and a stack of small anatomy icons, labelled 'other evidence: many genes, many body features', slide under the tree like a foundation.
scenes.narration: A shared, derived character can mark a clade. It is a new state that arose in a common ancestor. Moulting fits one origin on this tree. Cavity type changes several times. To test any character, lay it on a tree built from other evidence. Many genes are one such source.

scenes.tts: So keep two jobs apart. A body plan describes how an animal is built. Independent evidence tests whom it descends from.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left, the three cross-sections, label 'describes'; right, the gene tree, label 'tests ancestry'.
scenes.narration: So keep two jobs apart. A body plan describes how an animal is built. Independent evidence tests whom it descends from.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'A body plan describes an animal; independent evidence tests its ancestry.'
